Policy sheet (sorceress)

How the hero handles its chores. Set it once, change it any time. Poor choices are allowed: try them and read what they cost.

(U) marks a counter whose link to the setting is a guess, not a measurement. 'Not reported' means no event carries it yet.

Potion mix

What the four belt columns hold, so what the hero buys and refills in town. The default is the build's own plan (casters about half mana, a Barbarian no mana). Rejuvenation columns buy healing until the shop sells rejuvenation. docs/belt-plan.md.

default
your call No healing potion is bought; life can only be answered by the town portal and the walk home. Your call, risky.

How boldly the hero fights

How far the hero notices and chases monsters and how early it backs off. It moves existing fight settings together: how far away a monster is noticed, how long a chase lasts, the life lines for potions and for leaving the game, extra care against champions, and when the potion count sends the hero to town. A melee hero and a caster get different numbers for the same stance (sheet: Knobs).

Cautious: only fights what comes close (noticed within about 4 tiles for a melee hero, 5 for a caster), gives up a chase sooner, drinks a healing potion at 65 percent life, leaves the game at 35 percent, takes extra care with champions and goes to town when 3 healing potions are left.
Balanced: today's behaviour. Monsters within 6 tiles are fought, a healing potion at 55 percent life, the game is left at 25 percent, a town trip at 2 healing potions.default
Aggressive: goes after monsters from farther away (about 8 tiles for a melee hero, 7 for a caster), chases longer, drinks at 50 percent life, leaves the game at 22 percent (20 for a caster), takes less extra care with champions and goes to town only when 1 healing potion is left. A melee hero starts here: it has to walk up to its target.

Not changed. This row follows today's behaviour.
